issues.failure_explanation: For NtD maps, Lambda_sigma decreases in sigma (Property 2). With sigma_1=sigma_D <= sigma_2=sigma_bg, the middle term of (in1) is >= 0, but the stated upper bound int(sigma_1-sigma_2)|grad u_2|^2 is <= 0. In the opposite ordering the stated lower bound is >= 0 while the middle term is <= 0. So (in1) is false whenever sigma_1 != sigma_2 and grad u_2 != 0. The correct NtD inequality is int(sigma_2-sigma_1)|grad u_2|^2 <= <(Lambda_1-Lambda_2)g,g> <= int(sigma_2/sigma_1)(sigma_2-sigma_1)|grad u_2|^2. This is the form the paper itself uses in Section 6, and it also swaps which bound carries the factor sigma_2/sigma_1. The step (lem1), with the opposite sign, does not follow from (in1) as written.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace (in1) by the correct standard NtD inequality, as stated in Section 6, and derive (lem1) from its lower bound. The rest of the proof is unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: The cited 'well known inequality' is misstated, so the proof of Lemma 3.1 as written rests on a false premise. The lemma's conclusion and the bound (lem1) are true with the correct inequality.
issues.title: Inequality (in1) used in the proof of Lemma 3.1 is false as stated (wrong sign and weights); the derived bound does not follow from it
issues.why_classification: A local replacement of a standard inequality, already present in the paper, restores the proof with no change to the lemma or its uses.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: it is not possible to find a non-constant boundary data $g$ fulfilling~\eqref{eqn:idcond}

issues.failure_explanation: A is an arbitrary subset of Omega. If A is a single point or empty, 'u constant in A' is trivially true for any non-constant u, so the theorem is false as stated. A must be open, or of positive measure. The theorem also only covers n=2 with L^infty sigma and n=3 with Lipschitz sigma. The paper's standing assumptions are n>=2 and only sigma in L^infty_+. UCP for L^infty coefficients fails in dimension >=3. The conclusion that no nonzero g satisfies (idcond) is therefore only justified in the cases the theorem covers. The Section 2 assumptions do not guarantee this for the background sigma_bg.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State that A is a nonempty open set, and add the assumption that sigma_bg is Lipschitz for n>=3 (or restrict to n=2,3 as in the cited UCP results). Apply UCP to a connected component of D.
issues.overall_effect: The non-existence of an exact kernel element (the motivation for the approximate method) is established only under unstated extra hypotheses. In the numerics and examples sigma_bg is constant, so the method is not affected there.
issues.title: Weak UCP theorem stated with missing hypotheses on A and with a dimension/regularity scope narrower than the paper's setting
issues.why_classification: Adding the standard hypotheses (A open; background regularity and dimension) fixes the statement without changing the method or its conclusions.

issues.failure_explanation: The bound |lambda~_k - lambda_k| <= ||N|| for eigenvalues 'ordered in a decreasing order' is Weyl's min-max inequality. It needs both operators to be self-adjoint. A merely bounded N makes Lambda_n non-self-adjoint, possibly with complex eigenvalues, so the ordering is meaningless and the inequality can fail. N need not be compact either, so the k-th eigenvalue of Lambda_n need not exist. The numerical model symmetrizes N, which shows the needed hypothesis is omitted from the statement.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Assume N is bounded and self-adjoint, as in the numerical noise model, and state the result for the k-th largest min-max values of Lambda_n.
issues.overall_effect: The stated guarantee for noise-level reliability of eigenvalues is not valid for the noise class declared in the model; it holds for self-adjoint N.
issues.title: Eigenvalue perturbation bound stated for a general bounded noise operator N (self-adjointness missing)
issues.why_classification: A short added hypothesis already satisfied by the paper's own noise model preserves the proposition and its use.

issues.failure_explanation: From P-P_b <= int_D (sigma_bg/sigma_a)(sigma_bg-sigma_a)|grad u|^2 and (sigma_bg-sigma_a)/sigma_a <= (sigma_bg^M-sigma_a^m)/sigma_a^m, one obtains int_D sigma_bg|grad u|^2 >= sigma_a^m/(sigma_bg^M-sigma_a^m) (P-P_b). The paper's coefficient uses Delta_sigma = sigma_bg^m - sigma_a^M instead. Since sigma_bg^M-sigma_a^m >= Delta_sigma, with strict inequality for non-uniform sigma_bg or sigma_a, the claimed bound is strictly stronger than what is derivable. The two agree only for uniform sigma_bg and sigma_a.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the lower coefficient by sigma_a^m/(sigma_bg^M - sigma_a^m) and update the alpha-range and the Remark's condition (sufficiency of sigma_bg^m>sigma_a^m+sigma_a^M survives).
issues.overall_effect: The admissible range of alpha, (sigma_a^m/Delta, sigma_bg^M/Delta), is derived from an unsupported lower bound for non-uniform conductivities. The same constant enters the Remark's condition for alpha=1.
issues.title: Lower constant in (sogp3) does not follow from the stated bounds when conductivities are non-uniform
issues.why_classification: A one-line recomputation of a constant fixes it, and the remaining claims survive.

issues.failure_explanation: (sogp3) bounds the integral of the power density over D by constants times P-P_b. This says nothing about the level eps at which {sigma_bg|grad u|^2 < eps} approximates D. The quantity eps is a pointwise density, while alpha*lambda_n*||g_n||^2 is a total power, so the units differ. In the analytical example the sublevel set matching the integral condition has threshold eps = p(r~_i) = k*lambda_k/(pi*r~_i^2), not lambda_k. For sigma_a=1, sigma_bg=2, R=1, r_i=0.5, k=5, one has lambda_5 ~ 6.5e-5 and r~_5 ~ 0.48, so the correct threshold is ~4.5e-4. The 'educated guess' eps = lambda_k gives radius ~0.38. Section 5 actually used the integral condition, not this pointwise rule, so the Remark mischaracterizes it. The claim that clear bounds for admissible epsilon can be analytically derived is unsupported.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Drop the pointwise formula (thr) and its alpha-range. Define epsilon implicitly by the integral condition int_{p<eps} p = c*lambda_n*||g_n||^2, with c in the interval from (sogp3). State that the bounds justify only a constant-factor integral calibration.
issues.overall_effect: The threshold rule and its admissible range alpha are unreliable. The Section 4 procedure with epsilon(lambda_n, ||g_n||) has no valid calibration. Only the integral-level-set rule (thr2) with the sublevel-set procedure in the later Remark is consistent with the analysis.
issues.title: Pointwise power-density threshold epsilon = alpha*lambda_n*||g_n||^2 is derived from integral bounds and contradicts the analytical example
issues.why_classification: A contained replacement of the calibration rule by the integral condition already used in the paper suffices, but the promised analytic bounds on epsilon are withdrawn and weakened to constant-factor integral statements.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Identify the last eigenvalue $\overline{\lambda_k}$ of $\Lambda_n$ before the plateau and the corresponding eigenfunction $\overline{g_k}$
the eigenvalues of the perturbed operator plateauing when their amplitude is comparable with $\delta$

issues.failure_explanation: The identity P-P_b = <(Lambda_D-Lambda_bg)g_n,g_n> = lambda_n||g_n||^2 and the bounds (sogp3) were derived for eigenpairs of the noise-free operator. In the noisy algorithm, (lambda_bar, g_bar) is an eigenpair of Lambda_n = Lambda_D-Lambda_bg+N. The true power difference is lambda_bar||g_bar||^2 - <N g_bar, g_bar>, and |<N g_bar,g_bar>| can be as large as delta. Since lambda_bar is taken at the plateau, lambda_bar is of order delta, so the correction is comparable to the calibration value. The 'known' target power lambda_n||g_n||^2 can then be off by order one, or even have the wrong sign. No estimate of the effect on the reconstructed region is given.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Calibrate with the noise-corrected quantity, e.g. use the interval [lambda_bar - delta, lambda_bar + delta] in the bounds with delta known. Or choose g_bar with lambda_bar >> delta and quantify the error from <N g_bar, g_bar>. Restate the guarantee accordingly.
issues.overall_effect: The calibration condition in the final noisy-data algorithm has no supported accuracy statement, so the claimed robust reconstruction rule is unsubstantiated. Only the numerics support it.
issues.title: Noise-free power identity P-P_b = lambda_n||g_n||^2 reused for eigenpairs of the noisy operator at the noise plateau
issues.why_classification: A contained error analysis using the already available bound |<N g,g>|<=delta fixes it, at the cost of a weaker guarantee near the noise floor.
